title_tag: AI红利爆发，女性却“两头吃亏”：为什么她们既更难进高薪岗位，又更容易被替代？—— 英国《卫报》外刊讲解第1189天
h1: AI红利爆发，女性却“两头吃亏”：为什么她们既更难进高薪岗位，又更容易被替代？
category: 英国《卫报》外刊讲解 第1189天

headline.en_html: The AI industry is booming. Women are getting left behind — Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs but are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption
headline.zh: AI行业正在飞速发展，女性却被甩在后面——她们只占新增AI岗位的极小一部分，却在容易被AI冲击的岗位上占比过高。

notes.en: booming means growing or developing rapidly.
notes.zh: 蓬勃发展的、飞速增长的
notes.ctx: 标题第一个词就定下基调：这是“红利爆发”的行业——正因为它疯长，被落下的那部分人才格外刺眼。
notes.ex1: The AI industry is booming, but not everyone is benefiting. AI行业正在蓬勃发展，但并非人人受益。
notes.ex2: Tech hubs are booming across Asia. 亚洲各地的科技中心正在蓬勃发展。

notes.en: to be left behind means to be left in a position behind others, especially when they move forward.
notes.ctx: 被动语态是关键：不是女性自己不走，是别人往前跑的时候，她们被留在了原地。
notes.ex1: Workers who don't adapt will get left behind. 不适应变化的工人会被淘汰。
notes.ex2: Women are getting left behind in the AI boom. 女性正在AI热潮中被甩在后面。

notes.en: a fraction of means a very small part of something.
notes.zh: 极小一部分、微乎其微的比例
notes.ctx: fraction 是数学里的“分数”，用在人数上就是“零头”：新岗位一大把，女性只分到一撮。
notes.ex1: Women hold just a fraction of new AI jobs. 女性只占AI新岗位的极小一部分。
notes.ex2: The company spends only a fraction of its budget on training. 这家公司只把预算的极小一部分花在培训上。

notes.en: overrepresented means present in a group in a proportion higher than is usual or expected.
notes.ctx: 与前半句的 a fraction of 正好对照：好岗位里少得可怜，危险岗位里却多得异常——标题的“两头吃亏”就藏在这一对词里。
notes.ex1: Women are overrepresented in roles with high risk of AI disruption. 女性在容易被AI冲击的岗位上占比过高。
notes.ex2: The group is overrepresented in low-paying jobs. 该群体在低薪岗位中占比过高。

paragraphs.en_html: There’s a common fear among people who work in Silicon Valley: <mark class="voc">snag</mark> one of the fast-growing, high-paying jobs in artificial intelligence, or get trapped in the “<mark class="voc">permanent underclass</mark>”, a phrase describing the fate of those who won’t have <mark class="voc">upward mobility</mark> in the age of AI. The phrase usually describes a future in which AI <mark class="voc">automates</mark> human jobs. But for women in tech, <mark class="voc">it’s starting to look like the present</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 硅谷的职场人有一个共同的恐惧：要么抢到AI领域那些快速增长的高薪岗位，要么被困在“永久底层”——这个词描述的是在AI时代无法向上流动的那群人的命运。它通常被用来描述一个AI取代人类工作的未来。但对科技行业的女性来说，它开始看起来像是现在。

notes.en: snag means to get or obtain something, often quickly or by chance.
notes.ctx: 本义是“钩住、绊住”，用在求职上就成了“眼疾手快抢下来”：机会不是排队等来的，是从别人手里钩走的。
notes.ex1: She snagged one of the few AI jobs available. 她抢到了为数不多的AI岗位之一。
notes.ex2: He snagged a great deal on a used car. 他抢到了一辆二手车的划算买卖。

notes.en: permanent underclass means a group of people at the bottom of society who are unable to move up.
notes.ctx: permanent 是判决书上的词：不是暂时掉队，是这一辈子都上不去。文中指 AI 时代被卡在底层、再无上升通道的那群人。
notes.ex1: The phrase describes a future in which AI creates a permanent underclass. 这个词描述了一个AI制造出永久底层的未来。
notes.ex2: For women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present. 对科技女性来说，这开始像是现在。

notes.en: upward mobility means the ability to move to a higher social or economic class.
notes.ctx: 全文的价值尺度：一份工作值不值钱，看它能不能让人往上走，而不只看眼前那张工资条。
notes.ex1: AI could destroy upward mobility for many workers. AI可能摧毁许多工人的向上流动机会。
notes.ex2: Education is a key driver of upward mobility. 教育是向上流动的关键驱动力。

notes.en: automate means to make a process or job work by machines rather than people.
notes.zh: 使自动化、用机器取代人力
notes.ctx: 这里的主语是 AI、宾语是 human jobs——不是“帮人干活”，是“把整份活端走”，于是才有了下一句“谁被替代”的焦虑。
notes.ex1: AI is automating many human jobs. AI正在自动化许多人类工作。
notes.ex2: The factory has automated most of its production. 这家工厂已实现大部分生产自动化。

notes.w: it's starting to look like the present
notes.ipa: /ɪts ˈstɑːtɪŋ tə lʊk laɪk ðə ˈpreznt/
notes.en: it’s starting to look like the present means something that was expected in the future is now happening.
notes.zh: 开始看起来像现在、未来已来
notes.ctx: 全篇的第一次转折：本该属于“未来”的最坏设想，对科技行业的女性来说已经是“现在”，一句话把时态压平。
notes.ex1: For women in tech, the future of AI underclass is starting to look like the present. 对科技女性来说，AI底层的未来开始像现在。

paragraphs.en_html: “A lot of people say: ‘Oh, AI is <mark class="voc">lowering barriers</mark>, it’s <mark class="voc">equalizing the playing field</mark> for women,’” said Urvashi Batra, co-founder and CEO of Prioriwise, an AI platform for IT service providers. “I actually think it’s <mark class="voc">the opposite</mark>.” Batra said people <mark class="voc">take her less seriously</mark> as the founder of an AI company than her male co-founder. When <mark class="voc">pitching investors</mark>, she and her co-founder have learned that they are more likely to get an investment if he does the pitching.
paragraphs.zh: “很多人说：‘哦，AI在降低门槛，它在为女性创造公平的竞争环境。’”IT服务商的AI平台Prioriwise的联合创始人兼CEO Urvashi Batra说。“我恰恰认为，情况是相反的。”Batra说，作为AI公司的创始人，人们不如对待她的男联合创始人那样认真对待她。在向投资人路演时，她和她的联合创始人已经摸出一个规律：如果由他来路演，拿到投资的概率更大。

notes.en: lower barriers means to reduce the things that make it difficult to enter or succeed.
notes.ctx: 这是“AI对女性友好”论的全部依据：门槛低了，谁都能进。下文作者要用亲身经历推翻的，正是这一句。
notes.ex1: AI is said to lower barriers for women. 据说AI降低了女性的门槛。
notes.ex2: The policy aims to lower barriers to tech careers. 该政策旨在降低科技职业门槛。

notes.en: equalize the playing field means to make conditions fair for everyone.
notes.ctx: 原义是“把球场铲平”，指把先天条件拉齐。注意它与第 9 段的 a level playing field 是同一个比喻的两种说法。
notes.ex1: Many believe AI will equalize the playing field for women. 许多人认为AI会为女性创造公平竞争环境。
notes.ex2: The new law aims to equalize the playing field for small businesses. 新法律旨在为小企业创造公平竞争环境。

notes.en: the opposite means the completely different thing.
notes.ctx: 三个词顶掉前面一整套乐观论调：I actually think it’s the opposite——短、硬，还带一个 actually 表示“你们都想错了”。
notes.ex1: I actually think it’s the opposite. 我恰恰认为情况相反。
notes.ex2: The result was the opposite of what we expected. 结果与我们预期的恰恰相反。

notes.en: take someone seriously means to treat someone as important or worthy of attention.
notes.zh: 把某人当回事、重视某人
notes.ctx: 不是“没礼貌”，是专业判断被降级：同一个头衔，男联创被认真听，她被打折。
notes.ex1: People take her less seriously than her male co-founder. 人们不如对待她的男联合创始人那样认真对待她。
notes.ex2: We take all complaints seriously. 我们认真对待所有投诉。

notes.en: pitching investors means presenting a business idea to investors to get funding.
notes.zh: 向投资人路演、融资推介
notes.ctx: pitch 原指“投掷、摆摊叫卖”，融资场上就是拿着方案上台讲。“由他来讲更容易拿到钱”，一句话把性别折扣量化了。
notes.ex1: They learned they are more likely to get investment if he does the pitching. 他们发现如果由他来路演，更可能拿到投资。
notes.ex2: She pitched investors for two hours. 她向投资人路演了两个小时。

paragraphs.en_html: Women <mark class="voc">made up</mark> only about <mark class="voc">a quarter</mark> of new hires in AI roles in the last year, compared to 50% of new hires in non-AI roles, according to a recent report from LinkedIn. In <mark class="voc">executive roles</mark>, that number drops to just 13%. At the same time, LinkedIn’s research shows that women are more likely to work in roles with <mark class="voc">high exposure to AI disruption</mark>, like customer service, meaning they are also <mark class="voc">at higher risk for</mark> job loss due to AI.
paragraphs.zh: 根据LinkedIn最近的一份报告，过去一年AI岗位的新员工中，女性只占大约四分之一，而非AI岗位的新员工中，女性占了50%。在高管职位中，这个数字骤降到只有13%。与此同时，LinkedIn的研究显示，女性更可能从事那些高度暴露于AI冲击的岗位，比如客服，这意味着她们因AI而失业的风险也更高。

notes.en: make up means to form or constitute a part of something.
notes.ctx: 数据段的动词，后面接的都是比例：make up 后面跟数，问的就是“这块蛋糕里你占多少”。
notes.ex1: Women made up only about a quarter of new hires in AI roles. 女性只占AI新岗位的约四分之一。
notes.ex2: Immigrants make up a large part of the workforce. 移民占劳动力的很大一部分。

notes.en: a quarter means one fourth.
notes.ctx: 不写 25% 而写 a quarter，把冷数据说成“切走四分之一块”，紧接着的 50% 就形成了成倍的落差。
notes.ex1: Women made up about a quarter of AI new hires. 女性约占AI新员工的四分之一。
notes.ex2: A quarter of the students failed the exam. 四分之一的学生考试不及格。

notes.en: executive roles means positions at a senior management level.
notes.zh: 高管职位、高层管理岗位
notes.ctx: 从 25% 掉到 13% 的那一层：越往上走人越少，这就是“天花板”被量化后的样子。
notes.ex1: In executive roles, the number drops to just 13%. 在高管职位中，这个数字降到只有13%。
notes.ex2: She has held several executive roles. 她担任过多个高管职位。

notes.en: high exposure to AI disruption means being very likely to be affected by AI changes.
notes.ctx: exposure 是金融里的“敞口”：仓位越重，风一吹亏得越多。这里是“这份工作有多大比例真会被 AI 吃掉”。
notes.ex1: Women are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption. 女性更可能从事高度暴露于AI冲击的岗位。
notes.ex2: Customer service has high exposure to AI disruption. 客服岗位高度暴露于AI冲击。

notes.en: at higher risk for means more likely to experience something bad.
notes.zh: 面临更高风险、更容易遭遇
notes.ctx: 紧接 exposure 的落点：不是抽象的“受影响”，是具体的丢工作——风险从统计学变成了饭碗。
notes.ex1: They are at higher risk for job loss due to AI. 她们因AI而失业的风险更高。
notes.ex2: Smokers are at higher risk for lung cancer. 吸烟者患肺癌的风险更高。

paragraphs.en_html: AI jobs, whose postings have doubled since 2023, come with a <mark class="voc">salary premium</mark>, on average paying more than <mark class="voc">twice as much as</mark> roles that don’t involve working with AI. But women who do have jobs in AI are <mark class="voc">disproportionately</mark> concentrated in low-paying roles, like <mark class="voc">data annotators</mark>. Across all AI occupations, men have $45,000 higher <mark class="voc">median pay</mark> than women, <mark class="voc">partly due to</mark> the types of jobs they are likelier to have.
paragraphs.zh: AI岗位的招聘信息自2023年以来翻了一倍，而且带有薪资溢价，平均薪酬是不涉及AI的岗位的两倍多。但那些确实在AI行业工作的女性，却不成比例地集中在低薪岗位上，比如数据标注员。在所有AI职业中，男性的中位数薪酬比女性高45,000美元，部分原因在于他们更可能从事的那些岗位类型。

notes.en: salary premium means extra pay above the normal rate.
notes.ctx: premium 本是保险里的“保费”，本质是“为稀缺多付的钱”：AI 岗位贵，不是因为更辛苦，是因为会的人太少。
notes.ex1: AI jobs come with a salary premium. AI岗位带有薪资溢价。
notes.ex2: Workers with AI skills command a salary premium. 有AI技能的工人能获得薪资溢价。

notes.en: twice as much as means two times the amount.
notes.ctx: 先亮出溢价倍数，下一句才更扎心：同在一个两倍薪的行业里，女性却挤在最低薪的那一档。
notes.ex1: AI jobs pay more than twice as much as non-AI roles. AI岗位薪酬是非AI岗位的两倍多。
notes.ex2: She earns twice as much as her husband. 她挣的是她丈夫的两倍。

notes.en: disproportionately means in a way that is too large or too small compared to what is normal.
notes.zh: 不成比例地、占比过高（或过低）地
notes.ctx: 一个副词点破结构性偏差：不是“几个女性碰巧在低薪岗”，而是系统性地被挤在那里。
notes.ex1: Women are disproportionately concentrated in low-paying AI roles. 女性不成比例地集中在低薪AI岗位上。
notes.ex2: Minorities are disproportionately affected by the policy. 少数族裔受该政策影响不成比例地大。

notes.en: data annotators are people who label data to train AI.
notes.ctx: AI 行业最底层的工种：框猫、打标签、判断一句话是好是坏——教 AI 认世界的人，拿的却是最低的工资。
notes.ex1: Women are concentrated in roles like data annotators. 女性集中在数据标注员等岗位上。
notes.ex2: Data annotators are essential for training AI models. 数据标注员对训练AI模型至关重要。

notes.en: median pay is the middle value of all salaries.
notes.ctx: 用中位数而不是平均数，是为了排掉少数天价高管把均值拉高的干扰：4.5 万美元的差距，是“队伍正中间那个人”的差距。
notes.ex1: Men have $45,000 higher median pay than women in AI. 在AI行业，男性中位数薪酬比女性高4.5万美元。
notes.ex2: The median pay for the company is $60,000. 该公司中位数薪酬为6万美元。

notes.en: partly due to means partly because of.
notes.zh: 部分由于、部分原因在于
notes.ctx: 作者给自己留了余地：差距“部分”来自岗位类型——言下之意，还有一部分来自同岗不同酬。
notes.ex1: The gap is partly due to the types of jobs they have. 差距部分原因在于他们从事的岗位类型。
notes.ex2: The delay was partly due to bad weather. 延误部分是由于天气不好。

paragraphs.en_html: The <mark class="voc">ongoing</mark> trend could produce the greatest <mark class="voc">gender pay gap</mark> <mark class="voc">in generations</mark> and <mark class="voc">leave women out of</mark> building a technology that shaped the economy. “What we’re witnessing is a sort of <mark class="voc">backsliding</mark>,” said Brenda Darden Wilkerson, president of AnitaB.org, a non-profit devoted to advancing women in tech jobs.
paragraphs.zh: 这一持续的趋势可能造成几代人以来最大的性别薪酬差距，并让女性被排除在构建一种塑造了经济的技术之外。“我们正在目睹的，是一种倒退，”致力于推动女性从事科技工作的非营利组织AnitaB.org的主席Brenda Darden Wilkerson说。

notes.en: ongoing means continuing to happen.
notes.ctx: 强调这不是一次性事故，而是一条还在往前走的曲线——所以后果还可以更大。
notes.ex1: The ongoing trend could produce the greatest gender pay gap. 这一持续趋势可能造成最大的性别薪酬差距。
notes.ex2: The investigation is ongoing. 调查正在进行中。

notes.en: gender pay gap means the difference in pay between men and women.
notes.ctx: 用 gap（缝隙）而不是 difference，暗示这是一道裂开的口子，需要被 close——第 6 段的倡议就是来补这道缝的。
notes.ex1: The trend could produce the greatest gender pay gap in generations. 该趋势可能造成几代人以来最大的性别薪酬差距。
notes.ex2: The company is working to close the gender pay gap. 该公司正在努力缩小性别薪酬差距。

notes.en: in generations means for many generations.
notes.ctx: 这个短语是最高级的放大器：不是“这几年最糟”，是“好几辈人里最糟”。
notes.ex1: It could be the greatest gender pay gap in generations. 这可能是几代人以来最大的性别薪酬差距。
notes.ex2: This is the worst economic crisis in generations. 这是几代人以来最严重的经济危机。

notes.en: leave someone out of means to not include someone in something.
notes.zh: 把某人排除在外、让某人无法参与
notes.ctx: 与“明文禁止”不同，leave out 是“人就被漏在外面”：没人拦你，但就是没你的位置。
notes.ex1: It could leave women out of building a technology that shaped the economy. 这可能让女性被排除在构建一种塑造了经济的技术之外。
notes.ex2: She felt left out of the decision. 她觉得自己被排除在决策之外。

notes.en: backsliding means a return to bad habits or a worse situation.
notes.ctx: 原指“戒了又犯”，用在社会议题上就是“好不容易往前走的路又滑回去”，比 setback 更有画面感。
notes.ex1: What we’re witnessing is a sort of backsliding. 我们正在目睹的是一种倒退。
notes.ex2: The country is backsliding on human rights. 该国在人权方面正在倒退。

paragraphs.en_html: <mark class="voc">Initiatives</mark> to promote women in the tech industry have been ongoing for years, with <mark class="voc">mixed results</mark>. Women now hold about <mark class="voc">one-third</mark> of tech jobs in the US. But research has found that women leave the tech industry <mark class="voc">at a much higher rate than</mark> their male <mark class="voc">counterparts</mark>, citing factors like non-inclusive cultures and <mark class="voc">barriers to advancement</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 推动女性进入科技行业的各种倡议已经进行了多年，结果好坏参半。现在美国科技岗位中，女性占了大约三分之一。但研究发现，女性离开科技行业的速度远高于男性同行，给出的因素包括不包容的文化和晋升障碍。

notes.en: initiatives are new plans or actions to solve a problem.
notes.ctx: 指企业里各种“女性科技人才计划”之类的项目。作者先承认它们存在多年，紧接一句 mixed results 泼冷水。
notes.ex1: Initiatives to promote women in tech have been ongoing for years. 推动女性进入科技行业的倡议已进行多年。
notes.ex2: The government launched new initiatives to boost employment. 政府推出了促进就业的新举措。

notes.en: mixed results means some good and some bad outcomes.
notes.zh: 好坏参半的结果、成效不一
notes.ctx: 四个字否掉十几年的努力：进门的人数上去了，人却还是留不住。
notes.ex1: The initiatives have had mixed results. 这些倡议结果好坏参半。
notes.ex2: The policy produced mixed results. 该政策产生了好坏参半的结果。

notes.en: one-third means one part of three equal parts.
notes.ctx: 用分数而不是百分比，好跟上一段的“四分之一”对照：整体三分之一，AI 新岗位只有四分之一——新领域反而更窄。
notes.ex1: Women now hold about one-third of tech jobs in the US. 现在美国科技岗位中女性约占三分之一。
notes.ex2: One-third of the students passed. 三分之一的学生通过了。

notes.en: at a higher rate than means more frequently than.
notes.zh: 以高于……的比率、比……更频繁
notes.ctx: rate 强调频率：不是“有人走”，是“走的比例系统性地更高”，这才叫结构问题。
notes.ex1: Women leave tech at a much higher rate than men. 女性离开科技行业的速度远高于男性。
notes.ex2: Accidents occur at a higher rate in this area. 该地区事故发生率更高。

notes.en: counterpart means a person or thing with the same function in a different place.
notes.ctx: counter-（对应）+ part（角色）：说的是“同样位置上的另一个人”，不点明性别，你也听得懂是谁。
notes.ex1: Women leave tech at a higher rate than their male counterparts. 女性离开科技行业的速度高于男性同行。
notes.ex2: The minister met with his French counterpart. 部长会见了法国同行。

notes.en: barriers to advancement are things that prevent progress.
notes.zh: 晋升障碍、阻碍职业发展的因素
notes.ctx: 与标题里的 lower barriers 首尾呼应：门槛确实降了，可进门之后还有第二道坎。
notes.ex1: Factors include non-inclusive cultures and barriers to advancement. 因素包括不包容的文化和晋升障碍。
notes.ex2: The company removed barriers to advancement for women. 该公司消除了女性晋升的障碍。

paragraphs.en_html: Women working in AI may face even greater challenges. “AI moves extremely fast, and the pressure to keep up is <mark class="voc">immense</mark>,” said Jayeeta Putatunda, an AI engineering lead at investment firm Turing. “I have seen throughout my career so many amazing women I know kind of <mark class="voc">fall through the cracks</mark>.” Putatunda said it’s not uncommon to be the only female engineer on a team, and that when women are <mark class="voc">outnumbered</mark>, they have to <mark class="voc">speak up louder</mark> to make their ideas known. <mark class="voc">Mentorship</mark> in the AI field, especially by other women, can be hard to <mark class="voc">come by</mark>. And the <mark class="voc">breakneck pace</mark> of AI advancements means anyone working in the field should expect to put in long hours in order to keep up.
paragraphs.zh: 在AI行业工作的女性，可能面临更大的挑战。“AI发展极快，跟上的压力是巨大的，”投资公司Turing的AI工程负责人Jayeeta Putatunda说。“在我的整个职业生涯中，我见过太多我认识的优秀女性，某种程度上被漏掉了。”Putatunda说，在一个团队里成为唯一的女工程师并不罕见，而且当女性在人数上处于劣势时，她们必须更大声地说话才能让自己的想法被知道。AI领域的导师指导，尤其是来自其他女性的指导，很难获得。而AI进步的那种危险的高速，意味着在这个领域工作的人都应该预期要投入长时间才能跟上。

notes.en: immense means extremely large.
notes.ctx: 修饰 pressure：不是“有点累”，是压得人喘不过气的那种量级，与第 8 段的 overwhelming 前后接力。
notes.ex1: The pressure to keep up is immense. 跟上的压力是巨大的。
notes.ex2: She has immense talent. 她有巨大的天赋。

notes.en: fall through the cracks means to be missed or not noticed.
notes.ctx: 画面全在“缝”字上：系统不是故意筛掉她们，是她们从制度的缝隙里掉了下去，无声无息。
notes.ex1: So many amazing women fall through the cracks. 太多优秀女性被漏掉了。
notes.ex2: Some students fall through the cracks in large classes. 在大班里有些学生会被忽视。

notes.en: outnumbered means having fewer people than the other side.
notes.ctx: out-（超过）+ number（数目）：当“数量”本身成了权力，一个人的声音天生就被稀释。
notes.ex1: When women are outnumbered, they have to speak up louder. 当女性人数处于劣势时，她们必须更大声说话。
notes.ex2: The team was outnumbered by their opponents. 这支队伍人数少于对手。

notes.en: speak up louder means to express opinions more loudly or forcefully.
notes.zh: 更大声地说、更用力地表达意见
notes.ctx: 说是音量，其实是双重标准：同样的观点，她要说得更用力才被听见。
notes.ex1: They have to speak up louder to make their ideas known. 她们必须更大声说话才能让想法被知道。
notes.ex2: If you disagree, speak up. 如果你不同意，就说出来。

notes.en: mentorship is the guidance given by a mentor.
notes.ctx: -ship 后缀表“关系、身份”，mentorship 就是“有人带你”这件事本身；在 AI 这种新领域，它比学历更管用，却最难找。
notes.ex1: Mentorship in AI, especially by other women, is hard to come by. AI领域的导师指导，尤其是女性导师，很难获得。
notes.ex2: She credits her success to mentorship. 她把成功归功于导师指导。

notes.en: come by means to obtain or get something.
notes.ctx: 常与 hard 连用：hard to come by 是“求而不得”的固定说法，比 difficult to find 多一层“碰运气”的味道。
notes.ex1: Mentorship can be hard to come by. 导师指导很难获得。
notes.ex2: Jobs are hard to come by these days. 如今工作很难找。

notes.en: breakneck pace means extremely fast speed.
notes.zh: 危险的高速、极快的速度
notes.ctx: breakneck 字面是“会折断脖子的”，速度快到再快就要出事；用来形容 AI 迭代，暗含“跟不上就被甩下”。
notes.ex1: The breakneck pace of AI advancements means long hours. AI进步的危险高速意味着长时间工作。
notes.ex2: The company grew at breakneck pace. 公司以极快的速度增长。

paragraphs.en_html: Those kinds of work expectations can make it impossible for everyone to stay in the field. “I went on <mark class="voc">maternity leave</mark> for four months, and by the time I came back, there were completely different <mark class="voc">frameworks</mark> and levels of models,” Putatunda said. <mark class="voc">Getting caught back up</mark> was <mark class="voc">overwhelming</mark>. She said it was only possible with the help of supportive co-workers and a husband who <mark class="voc">equitably</mark> <mark class="voc">split childcare</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 那种工作预期会让每个人都无法留在这个领域。“我休了四个月产假，等我回来的时候，框架和模型层级已经完全变了，”Putatunda说。追赶上进度让人不堪重负。她说，只有靠支持她的同事和一个公平分担育儿的丈夫，这（追赶上进度）才成为可能。

notes.en: maternity leave is time off work for a mother to have a baby.
notes.ctx: 全篇唯一“只有女性会遇到”的变量：休假四个月，回来时整个行业已经换代。
notes.ex1: I went on maternity leave for four months. 我休了四个月产假。
notes.ex2: She is on maternity leave until June. 她休产假到六月。

notes.en: framework is a basic structure or set of ideas.
notes.ctx: 这里指技术框架：四个月不在，底层工具整套换掉——在 AI 行业，“经验”是会过期的。
notes.ex1: There were completely different frameworks and levels of models. 框架和模型层级已经完全变了。
notes.ex2: The company uses a new software framework. 该公司使用新的软件框架。

notes.en: get caught back up means to reach the same level as others after falling behind.
notes.ctx: catch up 是主动“追”，中间的 caught 是被动：不是她跑得快，是她被硬拽回队伍，代价极大。
notes.ex1: Getting caught back up was overwhelming. 追赶上进度让人不堪重负。
notes.ex2: She worked hard to get caught back up. 她努力工作以补上进度。

notes.en: overwhelming means very great or too much to handle.
notes.zh: 压倒性的、让人不堪重负的
notes.ctx: 与第 7 段的 immense 是同一副重担的两端：外面压力巨大，回来补课量也巨大。
notes.ex1: Getting caught back up was overwhelming. 追赶上进度让人不堪重负。
notes.ex2: The support was overwhelming. 支持是压倒性的。

notes.en: equitably means fairly and equally.
notes.ctx: 注意不是 equally（一人一半），而是 equitably（按需要分）：孩子的事没法五五开，公平比平均更现实。
notes.ex1: A husband who equitably split childcare. 一个公平分担育儿的丈夫。
notes.ex2: Resources should be distributed equitably. 资源应公平分配。

notes.en: split childcare means to share the responsibility of raising children.
notes.ctx: split 是“劈开、分成几份”：育儿不是“帮忙带一下”，是把责任切开、一人一半。
notes.ex1: Her husband equitably split childcare. 她丈夫公平分担育儿。
notes.ex2: Couples should split childcare equally. 夫妻应平等分担育儿。

paragraphs.en_html: The AI industry is so new and fast-moving that it should <mark class="voc">in theory</mark> be more <mark class="voc">meritocratic</mark>. No one has a decade of experience working with a model developed one year ago, which should mean everyone has <mark class="voc">a level playing field</mark>. But instead the field has <mark class="voc">indexed more on</mark> <mark class="voc">personal networks</mark> and other <mark class="voc">loose signals</mark>, according to some women who work in AI.
paragraphs.zh: AI行业如此之新、如此快速变化，以至于从理论上说，它应该更任人唯贤。没有人有十年经验去使用一个一年前才开发出来的模型，这应该意味着每个人都站在公平的起跑线上。但事实恰恰相反，根据一些在AI行业工作的女性的说法，这个领域更依赖于个人人脉和其他模糊信号。

notes.en: in theory means according to ideas, but not necessarily in reality.
notes.ctx: 作者故意只说 in theory、不说 in practice，答案留给下一句的 But instead——一个短语就把整段变成“理想 vs 现实”。
notes.ex1: In theory, it should be more meritocratic. 理论上，它应该更任人唯贤。
notes.ex2: In theory, the plan should work. 理论上，这个计划应该可行。

notes.en: meritocratic means based on ability and talent rather than class or money.
notes.zh: 任人唯贤的、凭本事说话的
notes.ctx: merit（功绩）+ -cracy（统治）：只看本事的系统，本该最偏爱新人——这正是本段反讽的起点。
notes.ex1: The AI industry should in theory be more meritocratic. AI行业理论上应更任人唯贤。
notes.ex2: The company claims to be meritocratic. 该公司声称任人唯贤。

notes.en: a level playing field means a fair situation for everyone.
notes.ctx: 与第 2 段 equalize the playing field 用的是同一个比喻，这次换成形容词 level：都在说“地要平”，可惜地从没平过。
notes.ex1: Everyone should have a level playing field. 每个人都应有公平竞争环境。
notes.ex2: The rules aim to create a level playing field. 规则旨在创造公平竞争环境。

notes.en: index on means to base or measure something on a particular thing.
notes.ctx: 金融里 index 是“挂钩、随某指数走”；说这个行业“挂在人脉上”，等于承认评判标准根本不在能力。
notes.ex1: The field has indexed more on personal networks. 这个领域更依赖个人人脉。
notes.ex2: Salaries are indexed on performance. 薪资以绩效为指标。

notes.en: personal networks are the people you know.
notes.ctx: 与“公开标准”相对：谁认识谁，比谁会什么更重要，而人脉恰好是女性最容易缺的那一项。
notes.ex1: The field relies on personal networks and loose signals. 这个领域依赖个人人脉和模糊信号。
notes.ex2: Building personal networks is important. 建立个人人脉很重要。

notes.en: loose signals are unclear or informal indicators.
notes.zh: 模糊信号、不明确的判断依据
notes.ctx: signal 是招聘里的“信号”，loose 是“松的”：标准一松，偏见就有缝可钻。
notes.ex1: It relies on personal networks and other loose signals. 它依赖个人人脉和其他模糊信号。
notes.ex2: Hiring should not rely on loose signals. 招聘不应依赖模糊信号。

paragraphs.en_html: The <mark class="voc">political climate</mark> has made it more challenging to get AI companies to support initiatives focused on women, said Felicia Newhouse, founder of AI Powered Women, an organization that promotes women’s participation and leadership in AI. Newhouse, a product marketer who has worked in technology companies for two decades, points to the <mark class="voc">Department of Justice</mark> targeting corporations with <mark class="voc">DEI programs</mark>, claiming the initiatives <mark class="voc">violate</mark> <mark class="voc">anti-discrimination laws</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 政治气候使得让AI公司支持聚焦女性的倡议变得更加困难，AI Powered Women的创始人Felicia Newhouse说。该组织致力于推动女性在AI领域的参与和领导力。Newhouse，一个在科技公司工作了二十年的产品营销人，指出美国司法部正在针对那些设有DEI项目的公司，声称这些倡议违反了反歧视法。

notes.en: political climate is the general political atmosphere.
notes.ctx: 用天气说政治：不是某一条法令，而是整片空气变了，企业连表态都要先看风向。
notes.ex1: The political climate has made it harder to support women. 政治气候使支持女性变得更难。
notes.ex2: The political climate is changing. 政治气候正在变化。

notes.en: the Department of Justice is the U.S. federal department responsible for law enforcement.
notes.ctx: 出现在这里不是普法，是给“企业不敢支持女性”找一个具体施压者：来告你歧视的，正是反歧视的执法者。
notes.ex1: The DOJ is targeting corporations with DEI programs. 美国司法部正在针对设有DEI项目的公司。
notes.ex2: The DOJ announced new charges. 司法部宣布了新指控。

notes.en: DEI programs are policies for diversity, equity, and inclusion.
notes.ctx: 三个字母是 diversity / equity / inclusion 的首字母。这类项目本是纠偏工具，如今反被指为“逆向歧视”。
notes.ex1: The DOJ claims DEI programs violate anti-discrimination laws. 司法部声称DEI项目违反反歧视法。
notes.ex2: Many companies have DEI programs. 许多公司有DEI项目。

notes.en: violate means to break a rule or law.
notes.ctx: 法律语境里的重词：一个动词，就把原本的“善意项目”定性成了“违法行为”。
notes.ex1: The initiatives violate anti-discrimination laws. 这些倡议违反反歧视法。
notes.ex2: The company violated safety rules. 该公司违反了安全规定。

notes.en: anti-discrimination laws are laws that prevent unfair treatment.
notes.ctx: 同一个词被两方使用：支持者说 DEI 是落实反歧视法，司法部说 DEI 违反反歧视法——词没变，立场全反。
notes.ex1: The initiatives allegedly violate anti-discrimination laws. 这些倡议被指违反反歧视法。
notes.ex2: Anti-discrimination laws protect workers. 反歧视法保护工人。

paragraphs.en_html: Still, she said the risk that women are left behind in the AI workforce was something that <mark class="voc">kept her up at night</mark>. “We’re talking about who <mark class="voc">captures</mark> a major new source of <mark class="voc">economic mobility</mark>,” she said. “The deepest risk is that a <mark class="voc">participation gap</mark> becomes a <mark class="voc">power gap</mark>.”
paragraphs.zh: 不过，她说，女性被落在AI劳动力之外的风险，是让她夜不能寐的事情。“我们在讨论的是谁将抓住一个重要的新经济流动来源，”她说。“最深层的风险是，参与差距会变成权力差距。”

notes.en: keep someone up at night means to make someone worry and unable to sleep.
notes.ctx: 全篇唯一的私人情绪：前面都是数据与引述，到这里收束成一个人的失眠。
notes.ex1: The risk kept her up at night. 这个风险让她夜不能寐。
notes.ex2: The thought of losing his job keeps him up at night. 失业的念头让他夜不能寐。

notes.en: captures means to take or get something.
notes.ctx: 宾语是“经济流动的来源”，等于把机会当成猎物：谁抓到，谁就往上走。
notes.ex1: Who captures a major new source of economic mobility. 谁抓住了一个重要的新经济流动来源。
notes.ex2: The company captured a large share of the market. 该公司占据了很大的市场份额。

notes.en: economic mobility means the ability to change one’s economic status.
notes.zh: 经济流动、经济地位的变化
notes.ctx: 与第 1 段的 upward mobility 前后扣合：AI 是新的上升电梯，问题在于女性究竟在不在电梯里。
notes.ex1: We’re talking about who captures a major new source of economic mobility. 我们在讨论谁抓住一个重要的新经济流动来源。
notes.ex2: Education can improve economic mobility. 教育可以改善经济流动。

notes.en: participation gap means the difference in who takes part.
notes.ctx: 不是能力差距，也不是兴趣差距，是“谁在里面、谁在外面”的差距——所以下一步才会滑向权力差距。
notes.ex1: The deepest risk is that a participation gap becomes a power gap. 最深层的风险是参与差距变成权力差距。
notes.ex2: The participation gap between men and women is widening. 男女参与差距正在扩大。

notes.en: power gap means the difference in power between groups.
notes.ctx: 收尾三个字：钱少只是表象，真正的问题是说话算不算数。与 participation gap 用同一句式接力。
notes.ex1: A participation gap becomes a power gap. 参与差距变成权力差距。
notes.ex2: The power gap between the rich and poor is growing. 贫富权力差距正在扩大。

proper.name: Silicon Valley / 硅谷
proper.def:
美国加州旧金山湾区南部，苹果、谷歌、OpenAI 等科技公司与 AI 高薪岗位最密集的地带，也是全球风险投资的大本营。
本文中的意思：文章用“硅谷职场人的共同恐惧”开场——要么抢到高薪 AI 岗，要么掉进永久底层，恐惧的发源地就在这里。

proper.name: Prioriwise
proper.def:
一家为 IT 服务提供商提供 AI 平台的公司，帮助企业通过 AI 发现数据价值。
本文中的意思：其联合创始人 Urvashi Batra 用融资时的亲身遭遇，说明“AI 让女性更公平”的说法站不住脚。

proper.name: Urvashi Batra
proper.def:
Prioriwise 的联合创始人兼 CEO，AI 行业女性创业者。
本文中的意思：她以自身经历说明，作为 AI 公司的女性创始人，她不如男联合创始人被认真对待，融资路演时需由男性出面更易成功。

proper.name: LinkedIn / 领英
proper.def:
全球最大的职业社交平台，同时也发布招聘与劳动力市场研究报告。
本文中的意思：文中第 3 段的数据来源——AI 新岗位中女性仅占约四分之一，高管层只剩 13%。

proper.name: World Economic Forum / 世界经济论坛
proper.def:
总部位于日内瓦的国际组织，每年发布《全球性别差距报告》。
本文中的意思：其 2026 年报告指出，AI 公司高管层女性仅占 13.3%，非 AI 岗位女性占 45.1%，为文中的落差提供了另一组坐标。

proper.name: data annotators / 数据标注员
proper.def:
给 AI 训练数据打标签的工人，门槛低、重复性高、工资低，是 AI 行业最底层的岗位之一。
本文中的意思：女性在 AI 行业不成比例地集中在数据标注等低薪岗位，进一步加剧了性别薪酬差距。

proper.name: AnitaB.org
proper.def:
由计算机科学家 Anita Borg 于 1987 年创立的非营利组织，致力于推动女性在科技领域的平等。
本文中的意思：其主席在文中把当前趋势定性为 a sort of backsliding（一种倒退）。

proper.name: Brenda Darden Wilkerson
proper.def:
AnitaB.org 的主席兼 CEO，芝加哥公立学校“全民计算机科学”项目的创始人。
本文中的意思：她那句“我们正在目睹一种倒退”，是全篇的定调之语。

proper.name: Jayeeta Putatunda
proper.def:
投资公司 Turing 的 AI 工程负责人，北美排名前 1% 的导师。
本文中的意思：她讲的三件事——团队里唯一的女工程师、导师难找、产假归来要重新追赶——撑起了第 7、8 两段的全部细节。

proper.name: Turing
proper.def:
美国 AI 公司，2018 年成立，2025 年估值达 22 亿美元，主营 AI 模型训练与企业 AI 系统。
本文中的意思：Putatunda 就职于此，她的经历代表了 AI 行业女性面对的普遍压力。

proper.name: Felicia Newhouse
proper.def:
AI Powered Women 的创始人，在科技公司工作二十年的产品营销人。
本文中的意思：她指出政治气候使 AI 公司更难支持聚焦女性的倡议，并点名司法部针对 DEI 项目的行动。

proper.name: AI Powered Women
proper.def:
致力于推动女性在 AI 领域参与度与领导力的组织。
本文中的意思：其创始人的判断解释了第 10 段的核心——不是企业不想做，是现在做有法律风险。

proper.name: DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion)
proper.def:
多元、公平、包容，美国企业与机构推行的政策组合，旨在提升少数族裔、女性等群体的代表性。
本文中的意思：这类项目本是纠偏工具，如今被司法部指为违反反歧视法，AI 公司因此不敢再资助女性倡议。

proper.name: Department of Justice (DOJ) / 美国司法部
proper.def:
美国联邦司法部，负责执法与司法行政。
本文中的意思：文中提到它盯上设有 DEI 项目的公司，声称这些项目违反反歧视法，给企业支持女性倡议带来政治压力。

proper.name: IBM / 德勤（Deloitte）
proper.def:
两家美国大型企业，因 DEI 项目与司法部达成和解：IBM 支付约 1700 万美元，德勤支付 2150 万美元。
本文中的意思：这两笔和解金就是“支持女性项目变得政治敏感”的价码，也是企业退缩的直接原因。

proper.name: Todd Blanche / Stanley Woodward
proper.def:
美国司法部长与副司法部长。

proper.name: Civil Rights Fraud Initiative / 民权欺诈倡议
proper.def:
2025 年 5 月美国司法部启动的项目，旨在调查 DEI 项目是否违反反歧视法。
本文中的意思：该倡议导致 IBM、德勤等公司被调查并和解，进一步抬高了 AI 公司支持女性倡议的政治成本。

sources_note: 资料核对：以上背景依据课件原文与正文内容整理，并参考 LinkedIn 2025 年 AI 岗位性别构成报告、世界经济论坛《全球性别差距报告》以及美国司法部 2025 年民权欺诈倡议相关公开信息。

practice.intro: 请将以下中文句子翻译为英文（参考答案见后）。
items: 硅谷人害怕被困在“永久底层”，而对科技行业的女性来说，这已经开始变成现实。
女性AI创始人发现，如果由男联合创始人去做路演，他们更容易拿到投资。
女性只占AI新岗位的四分之一和高管职位的13%，却更多从事容易被AI替代的工作。
AI岗位工资是非AI岗位的两倍多，但女性更多集中在数据标注这类低薪工作上。
AI行业理论上应该任人唯贤，但实际上更依赖人脉和模糊信号。
最深层的风险是，女性在AI领域的参与差距会变成权力差距。
practice.critical_en: If AI rewards speed and networks rather than credentials, it should be the fairest industry ever built — so why is it reproducing the oldest gender gap of all?
practice.critical_zh: 如果 AI 行业拼的是速度和应变、而不是资历，它本该是史上最公平的行业——那它为什么反而复制了最古老的那道性别鸿沟？
practice.answer:
1. Silicon Valley workers fear getting trapped in the “permanent underclass”, and for women in tech, it’s starting to look like the present.

2. Female AI founders have learned that they are more likely to get investment if their male co-founder does the pitching.

3. Women make up only a quarter of new AI hires and 13% of executives, but are more likely to work in roles with high exposure to AI disruption.

4. AI jobs pay more than twice as much as non-AI roles, but women are disproportionately concentrated in low-paying roles like data annotators.

5. The AI industry should in theory be meritocratic, but it relies more on personal networks and other loose signals.

6. The deepest risk is that a participation gap becomes a power gap.
